identification.summary: DAGGER PANDA is CrowdStrike's name for the activity Kaspersky publicly reported as Icefog; aggregators list RedFoxtrot and UAT-7290 as related or equivalent names, but those mappings rest on third-party vendor overlap statements, not on CrowdStrike text I could open [S1][S5][S6]. Kaspersky announced Icefog in September 2013 as a small group, active since 2011, focused on South Korea and Japan and on supply-chain attacks against defense contractors, shipbuilders, telecom and satellite operators and media companies [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Kaspersky: operation began in 2011 [S1]. Recorded Future dates RedFoxtrot activity to 2014 [S3]. Talos has tracked UAT-7290 since at least 2022 [S4].
identification.notes: Three vendor clusters are in play and must not be merged: Icefog (Kaspersky, 2013-2014) [S1][S2]; RedFoxtrot (Recorded Future, 2021), which Recorded Future says overlaps Temp.Trident and Nomad Panda [S3]; and UAT-7290 (Cisco Talos, 2026), which Talos says shares significant victimology, infrastructure and tooling overlap with Red Foxtrot [S4]. The Icefog-to-RedFoxtrot-to-UAT-7290 chain is therefore inferred through the encyclopedia's imported alias list and an aggregator page, not through a single primary document [S5]. Microsoft has no mapped name for this actor in this record.

attribution.sponsor: Recorded Future ties RedFoxtrot to PLA Unit 69010 in Urumqi, Xinjiang, assessed as likely a cover designator for a Technical Reconnaissance Bureau within the PLA Strategic Support Force Network Systems Department [S3]. No source I opened attributes Icefog itself to a state.
attribution.confidence: Recorded Future assessed with high confidence that RedFoxtrot is Chinese state-sponsored [S3]. Talos assessed with high confidence that UAT-7290 is China-nexus [S4]. Kaspersky described Icefog operators as likely based in China, South Korea and Japan and as a small mercenary-style team, an inference from behavior rather than confirmed tasking [S1][S2].
attribution.basis: Recorded Future: operator OPSEC lapse exposing the unit's headquarters address, plus procurement and court documents, and shared custom capabilities (as summarized in search results, not the full report) [S3]. Talos: victimology, infrastructure and tooling overlap with Red Foxtrot [S4]. Kaspersky: infrastructure IP lists [S1].

objectives: Espionage. Kaspersky said Icefog operators quickly took the information they wanted and left [S1]. Recorded Future reports RedFoxtrot collection against aerospace and defense, government, telecommunications, mining and research organizations [S3]. Talos describes UAT-7290 as espionage-motivated and also an initial-access provider building relay infrastructure other China-nexus actors can reuse [S4].

regions: United States oil and gas companies (Javafog, Jan 2014) [S2]
Afghanistan, India, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan (RedFoxtrot) [S3]
South Asia and Southeastern Europe telecoms (UAT-7290) [S4]
targeting.notes: Targeting differs by vendor cluster: East Asia and supply chain in 2013 [S1], Central/South Asia in 2021 [S3], South Asian and European telecoms in 2026 [S4].

capabilities.summary: Icefog: spear-phishing with exploits for known vulnerabilities (CVE-2012-0158, CVE-2013-0422 per search coverage of the Kaspersky report), backdoors for Windows and Mac OS X, and the Java-based Javafog; Kaspersky counted more than 4,000 unique infected IPs, including a few dozen Windows and over 350 Mac OS X victims [S1][S2][S5]. RedFoxtrot: custom and publicly available malware [S3]. UAT-7290: exploitation of one-day vulnerabilities in public-facing edge devices, target-specific SSH brute-forcing, public PoC code, Linux implants RushDrop (ChronosRAT), DriveSwitch and SilentRaid (MystRodX), and Windows RedLeaves and ShadowPad [S4].

campaigns.name: Icefog operation begins
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky dates the operation to 2011, focused on South Korea and Japan and supply-chain targets [S1].

campaigns.name: Kaspersky discloses Icefog
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky publishes the Icefog report describing hit-and-run espionage with Windows and Mac OS X backdoors [S1].

campaigns.name: Javafog against US energy companies
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky reports a Java backdoor variant targeting at least three US oil and gas companies [S2].

campaigns.name: Recorded Future reports RedFoxtrot
campaigns.summary: Insikt Group links RedFoxtrot to PLA Unit 69010 and reports targeting across Central and South Asia since 2014 [S3].

campaigns.name: Talos reports UAT-7290
campaigns.summary: Talos describes edge-device exploitation against South Asian and Southeastern European telecoms and notes overlap with Red Foxtrot [S4].

diamond.adversary: Small China-linked operator group (Icefog) [S1]; RedFoxtrot linked by Recorded Future to PLA Unit 69010 [S3]; UAT-7290 assessed China-nexus by Talos [S4].
diamond.capability: Spear-phishing, known-vulnerability exploits, cross-platform backdoors [S1][S5]; edge-device one-day exploitation and Linux implants in the 2026 cluster [S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Icefog C&C infrastructure with IP lists suggesting China, South Korea and Japan [S1]; UAT-7290 builds relay box infrastructure reusable by other actors [S4].
diamond.victim: East Asian defense, maritime, telecom and media firms [S1]; US oil and gas [S2]; Central and South Asian government, defense and telecom [S3]; South Asian and European telecoms [S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection supporting PRC defense and regional interests, with RedFoxtrot focus on bordering Asian countries per Recorded Future [S3].
diamond.technology: Windows, Mac OS X and Java hosts for Icefog [S1][S2]; internet-facing edge networking devices and Linux systems in telecom networks for UAT-7290 [S4].

gaps: Primary documents (Kaspersky Securelist reports, Talos UAT-7290 blog, Recorded Future RedFoxtrot report, CrowdStrike DAGGER PANDA profile) could not be fetched in this session; details rely on search-result summaries and the Kaspersky press release.
No CrowdStrike source mapping DAGGER PANDA to Icefog was opened; the mapping rests on the encyclopedia's imported MISP/Malpedia data.
The Icefog to RedFoxtrot to UAT-7290 lineage is inferred from vendor overlap statements; whether one organization operates all three is unconfirmed.
Icefog activity after 2014 and any direct state attribution of the original Icefog cluster are not established in sources gathered.
No Microsoft name or MITRE group ID is mapped.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Telecom networks, edge devices and defense-industrial supply chains in Asia are key terrain [S1][S4]. STEP 2: Operators exploit known vulnerabilities rather than zero-days, so patch latency is the adversary advantage [S1][S4]. STEP 3: Template is spear-phish or one-day edge exploit, then backdoor, targeted collection, rapid exit or relay-box use [S1][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued collection against regional telecom and defense targets. MDCOA is use of compromised telecom or edge infrastructure as relays for other China-nexus actors against allied networks [S4]. Candidate indicators: unpatched edge devices showing SSH brute-force, unexpected Linux implants on network appliances, and Mac OS X backdoors on staff of defense suppliers [S1][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track edge-device advisories and telecom-sector reporting for partner nations [S4]. (2) Authorities: partner and contractor networks sit outside DoDIN authorities; coordinate through DC3 and DIB cybersecurity channels. (3) Mission assurance: telecom and logistics suppliers in the Indo-Pacific are candidate dependencies to map [S1][S4]. (4) Coordination: because vendor names diverge, share indicators by technique and infrastructure rather than by group name.
